where: Section 2, application domain list item 5; also Figure and Worked example step 4
problem: The chapter defines 'product-line software' as libraries, frameworks and components reused across products, and gives a payment SDK as the example. Standard textbooks define product-line software as a family of related systems built from a common core with managed variation, not as a reuse library. The chapter also contradicts itself: the earlier bullet in the same section correctly says product lines are 'one core sold to many customers with configuration'. A student who writes 'libraries = product-line software' in an exam will lose marks.
fix: Product-line software: a family of related products built from one shared core with managed variation, for example a firm's three meter models from one firmware base. Reusable libraries, frameworks and SDKs are a separate reuse category (component-based reuse), not a product line. In the worked example and quiz, classify the 5 payment libraries as reusable components, and keep product-line separate.

where: Section 2, application domain list item 2 and item 6
problem: Web and mobile applications are called 'the largest modern sub-class' of application software, yet web and mobile is also listed as a domain of its own. A reader cannot tell whether the 25 web apps belong to one category or two.
fix: State one rule: web and mobile is a sub-class of application software; count each system once, under the sub-class it fits best.

where: Section 2 domain list (last bullet) and Quiz Q2 answer
problem: Legacy is presented as an application domain and is offered as an answer to 'name four application domains'. Legacy is a condition of software (old, still in production, still business-critical), not a grouping by who uses it or what it must do; a legacy payroll system is still application software. The Figure note that the payroll systems fall 'under legacy, not under application software' repeats this confusion.
fix: List the seven application domains (system, application, engineering/scientific, embedded, product-line, web/mobile, AI). Treat legacy as a separate label that can be attached to software in any domain, and say the payroll systems are application software that has become legacy.

where: Section 2, first paragraph (Software as a service)
problem: SaaS is described as 'the customer pays a subscription', but the example given, a GST filing portal billed per return, is usage-based pricing, not a subscription. The example contradicts the definition.
fix: Say the customer pays a recurring fee, by subscription or per use, and uses the vendor's running system, like a GST filing portal billed per return.

problem: The figure '80 percent third-party components' is presented as a fact with no source and varies widely by product. Vague numbers stated as facts should not appear.
fix: Say 'a large share of a modern product may be third-party components and open-source code' without the specific percentage.

problem: The wording 'give one difference each between system software and application software' is ambiguous; a student may think two differences are wanted, one for each, and waste time.
fix: Ask: 'State one difference between system software and application software, and give one example of each.'
